title: GMAT Focus Data Insights Practice Test 6
instructions: Original exam-style practice test with answers and explanations.

questions.prompt:
Annual loans and weekly opening hours at five libraries:

Ancroft: 41,200 loans, 52 hours
Bewley: 28,600 loans, 30 hours
Cranleigh: 63,400 loans, 84 hours
Denby Vale: 19,800 loans, 26 hours
Elmhurst: 35,100 loans, 39 hours

Which library issues the most loans per opening hour?
options: A. Ancroft
B. Bewley
C. Cranleigh
D. Denby Vale
E. Elmhurst
questions.explanation: Loans divided by hours: Ancroft 792, Bewley 953, Cranleigh 755, Denby Vale 762, Elmhurst 900. Bewley is highest. The busiest library by total loans also opens longest, so it is not the most intensively used hour by hour.

questions.prompt:
Quarterly electricity costs for a factory, in thousands:

Q1: 62.4
Q2: 71.8
Q3: 69.5
Q4: 84.1

In which quarter was the percentage rise over the previous quarter greatest?
options: A. Q3
B. Costs fell in every quarter
C. The rise was equal in each quarter
D. Q2
E. Q4
questions.explanation: Quarter on quarter: Q2 +15.1%, Q3 -3.2%, Q4 +21.0%. Q4 is largest at 21.0%. Q4 adds more in absolute terms but rises from a larger base.

questions.prompt:
A manufacturer's costs by category:

Wages: 46%
Materials: 24%
Premises: 12%
Transport: 9%
Insurance: 6%
Other: 3%

What is the smallest number of categories that together account for at least 90% of costs?
options: A. Four
B. Two
C. Three
D. Five
E. Six
questions.explanation: Largest first: 46 + 24 + 12 = 82%, short of 90. Adding Transport reaches 91%. So 4 categories are needed.

questions.prompt:
Eight measurements, in order: 31, 33, 34, 34, 36, 39, 41, 88

Which statement about these measurements is accurate?
options: A. The mean is smaller than the median
B. The mean and median are equal
C. The range is larger than the mean
D. The mean is more than twice the median
E. The mode is larger than the mean
questions.explanation: Mean 42.00, median 35, range 88 − 31 = 57. The range exceeds the mean; the mean exceeds the median but not by a factor of two, and the mode is 34.

questions.prompt:
Two broadband packages charge a monthly fee plus a rate for each gigabyte over the allowance:

Package One: GBP 12.00 a month plus GBP 1.80 a gigabyte
Package Two: GBP 30.00 a month plus GBP 0.60 a gigabyte

Select the excess usage at which the two cost the same AND the cheaper package at 25 gigabytes of excess.
options: A. 15 GB; Package One is cheaper at 25 GB
B. 10 GB; Package Two is cheaper at 25 GB
C. 15 GB; the two cost the same at 25 GB
D. 15 GB; Package Two is cheaper at 25 GB
E. The two never cost the same
questions.explanation: Equal when 12 + 1.8g = 30 + 0.6g, so g = 18/1.2 = 15 GB. At 25 GB: One costs GBP 57.00, Two costs GBP 45.00, so Package Two is cheaper above the crossover.

questions.prompt:
Equipment can be bought for GBP 7,200.00 with servicing of GBP 340.00 a year, or rented for GBP 260.00 a month with servicing included.

Over two years, select the cheaper option AND the amount saved.
options: A. Buying; GBP 1,640.00
B. Renting; GBP 1,640.00
C. Buying; GBP 500.00
D. Renting; GBP 1,000.00
E. The two cost the same over two years
questions.explanation: Buying over two years: GBP 7,200.00 + 2 × GBP 340.00 = GBP 7,880.00. Renting: 24 × GBP 260.00 = GBP 6,240.00. Renting is cheaper by GBP 1,640.00. Comparing the purchase price with one year of rent is the error.

questions.prompt:
Two branches last month:

Branch X: 1,840 transactions, average value GBP 26.50
Branch Y: 960 transactions, average value GBP 41.20

Select the branch with the higher total takings AND the branch with the higher average transaction.
options: A. Branch X on takings; Branch Y on average transaction
B. Branch X on both
C. Branch Y on takings; Branch X on average transaction
D. Branch Y on both
E. The two branches are equal on both measures
questions.explanation: Takings: Branch X GBP 48,760.00, Branch Y GBP 39,552.00. Average transaction is given directly: Branch X GBP 26.50, Branch Y GBP 41.20. Volume and value point to different branches, so neither figure alone ranks them.

questions.prompt:
A workshop has fixed costs of GBP 41,000.00. Each unit sells for GBP 340.00 and costs GBP 215.00 to make.

Select the number of units needed to break even AND the number needed to make a profit of GBP 25,000.00.
options: A. 328 to break even; 656 for the target
B. 300 to break even; 528 for the target
C. 328 to break even; 600 for the target
D. 328 to break even; 500 for the target
E. 328 to break even; 528 for the target
questions.explanation: Contribution is GBP 125.00 a unit. Break-even is GBP 41,000.00 / GBP 125.00 = 328 units. For GBP 25,000.00 of profit the workshop must cover GBP 66,000.00, needing 528 units.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): households — District A 12,400, District B 5,100, District C 8,800

SOURCE 2 (table): reported burglaries last year — District A 386, District B 214, District C 242

SOURCE 3 (memo): "Patrols should be increased where the rate per household is highest."

Which district should receive more patrols on that criterion?
options: A. District A
B. District B
C. District C
D. The three districts are equal
E. Cannot be determined from the sources
questions.explanation: Burglaries per thousand households: District A 31.1, District B 42.0, District C 27.5. District B is highest. District A reports the most burglaries in total and has by far the most households.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (memo): "Our staff survey shows 81% would recommend the company as a place to work."

SOURCE 2 (method note): "The survey was open for one week and completed voluntarily."

SOURCE 3 (table): 22% of staff completed it.

Which statement is best supported?
options: A. Fewer than a fifth of staff would recommend the company
B. The survey is worthless and should be repeated
C. The 81% describes the fifth of staff who chose to respond, and those who declined may differ systematically
D. Response rates below a quarter always indicate dissatisfaction
E. The survey period was too short to reach part-time staff
questions.explanation: Voluntary completion by 22% of staff means the figure describes respondents, not the workforce, and people with strong views are likelier to answer. Option A inverts the finding without evidence; option D states a rule the sources do not support.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): units sold — Product K 24,000, Product M 6,800, Product N 15,300

SOURCE 2 (table): return rate — Product K 1.9%, Product M 7.4%, Product N 3.1%

SOURCE 3 (email): "Each return costs the same to process, so tackle whichever product generates the most returns."

Which product should be tackled first?
options: A. Product M
B. Product K
C. Product N
D. All three generate equal returns
E. Cannot be determined from the sources
questions.explanation: Returned units are sales multiplied by rate: Product K 456, Product M 503, Product N 474. Product M is highest. Product M has much the worst rate but sells too few units to top the count.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (report): "Output per worker rose 6% last year."

SOURCE 2 (table): the workforce fell from 480 to 405 over the same year.

SOURCE 3 (email): "The board is interested in total output."

Which statement is best supported for the measure the board wants?
options: A. Total output rose by 6%
B. Total output was unchanged
C. Total output rose by about 12%
D. Total output fell, because the workforce shrank by more than productivity grew
E. Total output cannot be estimated from these sources
questions.explanation: Total output is workers multiplied by output per worker: 405/480 = 0.844, and 0.844 × 1.06 = 0.894, about a 10.6% fall. Source 1 alone supports option A, which is why the headcount table is decisive.

questions.prompt:
A crate holds only large and small jars, 60 jars in all. How many are large?

(1) There are more small jars than large ones.
(2) The small jars outnumber the large ones by 24.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: (1) only tells us large is fewer than 30, which allows many values. (2) gives s − l = 24 with s + l = 60, so l = 18 — sufficient alone.

questions.prompt:
What is the value of a company's stock at year end?

(1) It held 4,200 units valued at GBP 15.00 each.
(2) Stock was one seventh of the GBP 441,000.00 total current assets.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: (1) gives 4,200 × GBP 15.00 = GBP 63,000.00 — sufficient. (2) gives GBP 441,000.00 / 7 = GBP 63,000.00 — also sufficient, and the two agree.

questions.prompt:
How long did a journey take?

(1) The average speed was 72 km/h.
(2) The distance covered was 198 km.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: Time is distance divided by speed, so neither figure alone is enough. Together, 198 / 72 = 2.75 hours — sufficient only in combination.

questions.prompt:
Is the median of five positive integers greater than 20?

(1) Their mean is 24.
(2) The largest is 60.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: A mean of 24 means they total 120. That is consistent with 1, 2, 3, 54, 60 (median 3) and with 20, 21, 22, 23, 34 — and adding that the largest is 60 still allows 1, 2, 3, 54, 60. The median is not pinned down.

questions.prompt:
Which site produces the highest output value per member of staff?

Site | Staff | Absence rate | Annual output value | Training score
Ardsley | 92 | 3.4% | GBP 148,000.00 | 82
Bramham | 148 | 2.1% | GBP 226,000.00 | 68
Cawood | 63 | 5.2% | GBP 97,000.00 | 91
Dinnington | 121 | 2.8% | GBP 189,000.00 | 75
Eccleshall | 176 | 1.6% | GBP 268,000.00 | 70
Ferrybridge | 108 | 4.1% | GBP 163,000.00 | 86
options: A. Bramham
B. Cawood
C. Ardsley
D. Dinnington
E. Eccleshall
questions.explanation: Output divided by staff: Ardsley GBP 1,608.70, Bramham GBP 1,527.03, Cawood GBP 1,539.68, Dinnington GBP 1,561.98, Eccleshall GBP 1,522.73, Ferrybridge GBP 1,509.26. Ardsley is highest. The site with the largest total output also has the most staff.

questions.prompt:
How many sites have an absence rate above the mean for the six?

Site | Staff | Absence rate | Annual output value | Training score
Ardsley | 92 | 3.4% | GBP 148,000.00 | 82
Bramham | 148 | 2.1% | GBP 226,000.00 | 68
Cawood | 63 | 5.2% | GBP 97,000.00 | 91
Dinnington | 121 | 2.8% | GBP 189,000.00 | 75
Eccleshall | 176 | 1.6% | GBP 268,000.00 | 70
Ferrybridge | 108 | 4.1% | GBP 163,000.00 | 86
options: A. One
B. Two
C. Four
D. Three
E. Five
questions.explanation: Mean absence is (3.4 + 2.1 + 5.2 + 2.8 + 1.6 + 4.1) / 6 = 3.20%. Above it: Ardsley 3.4%, Cawood 5.2%, Ferrybridge 4.1% — 3 sites.

questions.prompt:
Assuming 225 working days a year for each employee, which site loses the greatest number of days to absence?

Site | Staff | Absence rate | Annual output value | Training score
Ardsley | 92 | 3.4% | GBP 148,000.00 | 82
Bramham | 148 | 2.1% | GBP 226,000.00 | 68
Cawood | 63 | 5.2% | GBP 97,000.00 | 91
Dinnington | 121 | 2.8% | GBP 189,000.00 | 75
Eccleshall | 176 | 1.6% | GBP 268,000.00 | 70
Ferrybridge | 108 | 4.1% | GBP 163,000.00 | 86
options: A. Ferrybridge
B. Ardsley
C. Bramham
D. Cawood
E. Dinnington
questions.explanation: Days lost are staff × 225 × absence rate: Ardsley 704, Bramham 699, Cawood 737, Dinnington 762, Eccleshall 634, Ferrybridge 996. Ferrybridge is highest. The worst absence rate belongs to Cawood, which has too few staff to lead on days lost.

questions.prompt:
Rank the sites by output value and separately by training score, highest first in each. Which site's two ranks differ most?

Site | Staff | Absence rate | Annual output value | Training score
Ardsley | 92 | 3.4% | GBP 148,000.00 | 82
Bramham | 148 | 2.1% | GBP 226,000.00 | 68
Cawood | 63 | 5.2% | GBP 97,000.00 | 91
Dinnington | 121 | 2.8% | GBP 189,000.00 | 75
Eccleshall | 176 | 1.6% | GBP 268,000.00 | 70
Ferrybridge | 108 | 4.1% | GBP 163,000.00 | 86
options: A. Ardsley
B. Bramham
C. Dinnington
D. Ferrybridge
E. Cawood
questions.explanation: By output: Eccleshall, Bramham, Dinnington, Ferrybridge, Ardsley, Cawood. By training score: Cawood, Ferrybridge, Ardsley, Dinnington, Eccleshall, Bramham. Rank gaps: Ardsley 2, Bramham 4, Cawood 5, Dinnington 1, Eccleshall 4, Ferrybridge 2. Cawood differs by 5.
